title: Small generating trivial cofibrations for the Joyal model
statement: Use the Joyal model structure and universes of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. In each universe there is a small set $J_{\mathrm J}$ of monomorphisms of simplicial sets, each a categorical equivalence, such that the maps having the right lifting property against $J_{\mathrm J}$ are exactly the Joyal fibrations. Thus the trivial-cofibration weak-factorization system of the Joyal model is generated by a set (together with the boundary generators for monomorphisms); no Kan-enrichment hypothesis is part of this assertion.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, construction of the Joyal model structure and its generating trivial cofibrations; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Work in a fixed universe and let $\mathcal A=\mathsf{sSet}$, $C$ be the class of degreewise injective maps, and $W$ the class of categorical equivalences in the convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Simplicial sets are presheaves on the small simplex category, so [lem-coef-presheaf-local-presentability] gives local presentability; limits and colimits are computed degreewise, hence $\mathcal A$ is complete and cocomplete. The Joyal model-structure node identifies $C$ with its cofibrations and $W$ with its weak equivalences, and gives two-out-of-three and the two weak factorization systems.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1 and the presheaf description of simplicial sets; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: The relative boundary-cell presentation [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] says that every member of $C$ is a transfinite composite of pushouts of small coproducts of boundary inclusions. Boundary inclusions are themselves degreewise injective, and degreewise injective maps are closed under isomorphisms, pushouts, continuous transfinite composites and arrow retracts. A pushout of a coproduct $\coprod_{s\in S}(\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n)$ is, after well-ordering the small set $S$, the continuous transfinite composite of the single pushouts of $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ attached one at a time (at a limit stage take the union of the earlier stages), so it lies in the weakly saturated closure of the boundary inclusions; so does the $\omega$-composite $Z_0\to\operatorname{colim}_nZ_n$. Conversely a degreewise colimit of a chain of injections of sets is injective, which gives closure of $C$ under transfinite composites. Therefore $C$ is exactly the weakly saturated class generated by the small family of all boundary inclusions (one for each $n\geq0$).

source.place: Proposition 1.5.5.14, proof of (b), relative skeletal filtration; Kerodon source WANTED.

proof.text: The class $W$ is closed under filtered colimits by [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences]. The node [lem-coef-categorical-equivalences-small-generation] supplies a small set $E_0\subseteq W$ such that every categorical equivalence is isomorphic in the arrow category to a small filtered colimit of arrows from $E_0$. Take $\lambda=\aleph_0$: an $\aleph_0$-filtered diagram is a filtered one, and a filtered colimit in the arrow category is the colimit map of a natural transformation $a:X\to Y$ of filtered diagrams, which is the form of [lem-coef-joyal-filtered-equivalences]. Thus the full arrow subcategory on $W$ is accessible in the sense required by [lem-coef-smith-small-saturated-intersection].

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, proof (1), perfectness condition (4), and Proposition 2.2.5.8; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Let $F$ be the Joyal fibrations. By [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], the trivial cofibrations are exactly ${}^{\square}F$, and this class is $C\cap W$. The left lifting class closure [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and the transfinite-composition lemma [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting] show that ${}^{\square}F=C\cap W$ is weakly saturated, including pushouts, compositions, continuous transfinite composites, isomorphisms and arrow retracts.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, weak factorization systems; closure under lifting operations supplied by the cited DAG lemmas.

proof.text: If a map has the right lifting property against every member of $C$, then it is in the right class of the $(C,\text{trivial fibrations})$ weak factorization system of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Hence it is a trivial fibration and therefore belongs to $W$. This verifies the final Smith-recognition hypothesis for $C$.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1, first weak factorization system; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-smith-small-saturated-intersection] to $\mathcal A,C,W$. Steps 1--4 verify its local-presentability, small-generation of $C$, weak-saturation of $C\cap W$, filtered accessibility of $W$, and two-out-of-three hypotheses. It produces a small family $J_{\mathrm J}\subseteq C\cap W$ whose weakly saturated closure is $C\cap W$. Every member is therefore a monomorphism and a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, small generators for the saturated intersection; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: For any map $p$ having the right lifting property against every member of $J_{\mathrm J}$, we have $p\in J_{\mathrm J}^{\square}$. By [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure] and [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting], the class ${}^{\square}(J_{\mathrm J}^{\square})$ is closed under isomorphisms, pushouts, compositions, continuous transfinite composites and arrow retracts. Hence every map in the weakly saturated closure of $J_{\mathrm J}$ has the left lifting property against $p$, so $p$ has the right lifting property against every map in that closure. Since $J_{\mathrm J}$ weakly saturates to $C\cap W$, right lifting against $J_{\mathrm J}$ is exactly right lifting against $C\cap W$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, generator-to-saturation lifting argument; online PDF, archival source WANTED.

proof.text: The second weak factorization system in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] identifies the maps with the right lifting property against $C\cap W$ with the Joyal fibrations. Combining this identification with step 7 gives the asserted characterization by $J_{\mathrm J}$. The construction uses ordinary weak factorization systems and degreewise simplicial-set colimits; no Kan enrichment hypothesis is introduced. Adding the boundary generators from step 2 gives the cofibration/trivial-fibration system generated by sets as well.
